newsitem.title: USA: US stocks end a trace lower ahead of key jobs data.
newsitem.headline: US stocks end a trace lower ahead of key jobs data.

text.p: U.S. blue chips finished slightly lower on Thursday as investors adopted a guarded posture on the day before the release of critical monthly data on payrolls and wages.
The Dow industrials closed unofficially at 6945, down about one point. Broader indices also ended lower.

"It's amazing the Dow wasn't down more," said Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney. "You just didn't have any buyers today because you've got the moment of truth of the week tomorrow."
The session marked a reversal from Wednesday, when soothing comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan eased frayed nerves and returned a measure of confidence to the stock market.

But any exuberance that had been evident was absent on Thursday, as investors braced for the possibility of a strong set of employment figures, which could well prompt the Fed to set in motion an interest rate increase.
"The stock market is struggling to get a true sense of the strength of the economy and what will be the course of Fed policy," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates.

According to economists surveyed by Reuters, the report is expected to show 230,000 new jobs were created in February, down from 271,000 in January. The nation's unemployment rate is expected to edge down to 5.3 percent from 5.4 percent.
Analysts said the average hourly wage component of the report may hold the key. The figure is seen rising by 0.4 percent, up from 0.1 percent the previous month.
"Nobody's doubting that the labor market is tight," White said. "Our focus will be on the wage number."
While the overall mood was tentative, some sectors managed to stand out.
Oil companies were among the strongest performers. Texaco Inc rose 2-1/8 to 103-7/8 to lead Dow gainers. Chevron Corp, another Dow component, rose 1-1/8 to 66-1/2.
Tech stocks were weaker, resulting in a steeper decline in the Nasdaq Composite than other broad indices.
Oracle Corp skidded 3-3/16 to 36-9/16 after UBS Securities analyst Joseph Farley cut his rating on the shares to hold from strong buy, citing uncertainty about Oracle's fiscal third-quarter results.
The technology sell-off extended well beyond individual issues, however, dragging down a host of top-tier names.
Intel Corp fell 4-1/8 to 145-3/8, Microsoft Corp slipped 3-1/8 to 97-3/4, Cisco Systems Inc shed 2-1/4 to 54-5/8 and Dell Computer Corp dipped 1-1/4 to 73-7/8.
Great Western Financial Corp rose 1-3/4 to 46-3/4 after agreeing to be acquired by Washington Mutual Savings Bank in a friendly $6.6 billion deal.

Washington Mutual's offer tops a $6.1 billion hostile bid by A.H. Ahmanson and Co. Ahmanson, the nation's largest savings and loan, said it was still committed to the deal, and analysts expect the company to raise its bid.
Shares in Ahmanson fell 1-1/4 to 40-3/4. Washington Mutual shares fell 1/4 to 53.
The S&P 500 index fell 3.43 points to 798.56.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 13.66 points to 1315.43.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
